born November 15, 1983) is a Serbian-Montenegrin{{cite web|title=Sasha Pavlovic Player Profile|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=ANE|work=euroleague.net|access-date=14 March 2014}}{{cite web|title=Aleksandar Pavlović Profile |url=http://www.kkpartizan.rs/en/players-aleksandar-pavlovic.php |work=kkpartizan.rs |access-date=14 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140321213409/http://www.kkpartizan.rs/en/players-aleksandar-pavlovic.php |archive-date=21 March 2014 }} [[basketball]] executive and former professional player who spent ten seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), playing for the [[Utah Jazz]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]], [[Boston Celtics]] and the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He also represented the [[Serbia national basketball team|national basketball team of Serbia and Montenegro]] internationally. Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=7}}, he played the [[small forward]] and [[shooting guard]] positions. ==Professional career== ===Budućnost Podgorica (2000–2003)=== In his first professional season for [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]], Pavlović played in 14 games in the [[YUBA League]] and averaged 1.4 points per game. In his second season, Pavlović played in three games in the YUBA League and averaged 6.7 points. Also, Pavlović played two games in the [[EuroLeague]]. In his last season in Podgorica, Pavlović played in 20 games in the YUBA League and averaged 10.1 points and 2.4 rebounds per game. Pavlović averaged 9.6 points on 54% shooting for Budućnost in the EuroLeague, including a season-high 21 points against [[Tau Ceramica]]. ===Utah Jazz (2003–2004)=== Pavlović was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 19th pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]]. His American agent Marc Cornstein issued a clarification in response to a misleading [[Eurobasket.com]] biography mixing Aleksandar Pavlović with an 'Aleksander Pavlović' who played college basketball at [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle University]] and [[Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania]].{{cite news|last=Buckley|first=Tim|date=June 29, 2003|title=Is Sasha for real?|work=DeseretNews.com|url=https://www.deseret.com/2003/6/29/19731967/is-sasha-for-real|access-date=October 18, 2020}} In 79 games played (14 starts), Pavlović averaged 4.8 points and 2.0 rebounds. He scored a season-high 18 points on December 3, 2003, against the [[Houston Rockets]] and grabbed nine rebounds on two occasions. ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2004–2009)=== [[File:Cavs bench nov 2006 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Pavlović (left) with the Cavaliers alongside [[LeBron James]] and [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]] in 2006]] Pavlović was selected by the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]] in the [[expansion draft]] on June 22, 2004,{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/features/expansion_draft2004.html |title=NBA.com – 2004 Expansion Draft: Building the Bobcats |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2014-02-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100629164358/http://www.nba.com/features/expansion_draft2004.html |archive-date=2010-06-29 |url-status=dead }} and was traded to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for a [[Jared Dudley|2007 first-round draft pick]] the next day.[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/press_release_trades_062304.html Bobcats Acquire Draft Picks In Two Trades] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100321141603/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/press_release_trades_062304.html |date=2010-03-21 }} In 65 games played (nine starts), Pavlović averaged 4.8 points and 1.1 rebounds. He scored a season high 17 points on two occasions and scored in double digits on nine occasions.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/pavloal01/gamelog/2005/ Sasha Pavlovic 2004-05 Game Log] In 53 games of the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]], he started 19 times and averaged 4.5 points and 1.5 rebounds. He scored a season high 21 points on February 21, 2006, against the [[Orlando Magic]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20201021092100/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=260221005 LeBron scores 26 for Cavs; Darko gets 2 in Magic debut] Pavlović played three minutes over three playoff games and recorded only one rebound. In 67 games played (28 starts) in [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07]], Pavlović averaged a career-high 9.0 points, along with 2.4 rebounds and 1.6 assists. He scored 20 points or more on seven occasions, including a new career-high 25 points on March 13, 2007, against the [[Sacramento Kings]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20201020040436/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270313005 Pavlovic, Hughes make up for LeBron's absence in rout] Approximately two weeks later, Pavlović had a career-high six three-point field goals made (of 7 attempts) against the [[New York Knicks]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20201018161504/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270328018 Knicks holds off Cavs to keep playoff hopes alive] After occasional starts in the beginning of 2007, Pavlović was installed as the Cavaliers' starting shooting guard on March 1, 2007, and started the remaining 24 regular season games. As a starter, Pavlović averaged 12.7 points, 3.0 rebounds and 2.3 assists. Pavlović started all 20 of Cavaliers' 2007 playoff games. He had playoff highs of 17 points in a game 2 victory over the [[New Jersey Nets]] in the Eastern Conference Semifinals[https://web.archive.org/web/20201018161517/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270508005 LeBron kicks into next gear in 2nd half to power Cavs past Nets] and nine rebounds in a game 5 overtime victory over the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the Eastern Conference Finals.[https://web.archive.org/web/20170128063702/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270531008 LeBron bewilders Pistons as Cavaliers inch closer to NBA finals] In the 2007 offseason Pavlović was a [[restricted free agent]]. On October 30, 2007, after nearly a month's holdout he signed a three-year, $13.7 million extension with the Cavaliers.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3087179 Pavlovic ends holdout, agrees to three-year deal with Cavs] Pavlović injured his left foot on January 23, 2008, in a game against the [[Washington Wizards]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20201018083847/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280123005 Wizards give woeful effort as Cavs' Ilgauskas doesn't miss a shot][https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3212963 Pavlovic could miss up to 2 months with sprained left foot] He returned against the [[New Jersey Nets]] on March 12.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3289850 Undermanned Cavaliers welcome Pavlovic back into lineup] He started but was held scoreless in 9 minutes of action.[https://web.archive.org/web/20210308112010/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280312017 James moves into 2nd on Cavs' scoring list, but Nets end slump] On March 14, Pavlović had a season-high 24 points on against the Washington Wizards.[https://web.archive.org/web/20171008181056/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=280313027 Butler returns as Wizards dodge Cavs, get back to .500] He and scored double-digit points in 15 total games.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/pavloal01/gamelog/2008/ Sasha Pavlovic 2007-08 Game Log] During the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]], Pavlović played in 51 games (45 starts) and averaged 7.4 points, a career-high 2.5 rebounds and a career high 1.6 assists. In eight playoff games, he averaged 3.5 points and 1.3 rebounds. In the following [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]], the Cavaliers were beaten by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the 2009 Eastern Conference Finals, 4 games to 2. Pavlović became trade bait as talks with the [[Phoenix Suns]] were rekindled from earlier in the season and on June 25, 2009, he, [[Ben Wallace (basketball)|Ben Wallace]], and the 46th overall pick were traded to Phoenix for future teammate [[Shaquille O'Neal]].{{cite web| url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/shaq_traded_090625.html |title=Suns Complete Trade With Cavs, Send Shaq to Cleveland |date=June 25, 2009 |work=NBA.com |access-date=October 18, 2020}} On September 14, 2009, he was bought out by the Suns.{{cite web| url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/pavlovic_buyout_091409.html |title=Suns Buy Out Pavlovic |date=September 14, 2009 |work=NBA.com |access-date=October 18, 2020}} While playing for the Cavaliers, he bought a BMW car from [[LeBron James]]. There was an urban legend in Serbia that Pavlović won the car after beating him in one-on-one match, but Pavlović told in an interview that no such match was played.{{cite web |url=https://sportklub.rs/blog/jelena-trajkovic/a153947-Pavlovic-za-SK-Nisam-igrao-1-na-1-sa-Lebronom-za-auto/ |title=Pavlović za SK: Nisam igrao 1 na 1 sa Lebronom za auto |trans-title=Pavlović for SK: "I didn't play one-on-one with LeBron for the car" |author=Jelena Trajković |date=June 1, 2017 |website=sportklub.rs |publisher=Sport klub |access-date=June 13, 2022 |quote=Near the end of interview}} In another interview on January 2, 2020, he revealed that he still owns the car.{{cite web |url=https://www.kurir.rs/sport/kosarka/3385013/sasa-pavlovic-jos-vozim-lebronov-bmw-nije-mi-uvalio-krs |title=SAŠA PAVLOVIĆ: Još vozim Lebronov BMW, nije mi uvalio krš! |trans-title=Pavlović: I still drive LeBron's BMW, he didn't sold me a banger. |author=Predrag Gajić |date=January 2, 2020 |website=kurir.rs |publisher=Kurir |access-date=June 13, 2022 |quote=Middle of interview |language=Serbian}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2009–2010)=== On September 17, 2009, Pavlović signed a one-year, $1.5 million contract with the Minnesota Timberwolves.{{cite web| url =https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Wolves_Sign_Guard_Sasha_Pavlovic_2009_09_17.html | title = Wolves Sign Guard Sasha Pavlovic | work = NBA.com | date = September 17, 2009 | access-date = October 18, 2020}} In 71 games, he averaged 3.7 points per game. ===Multiple short stints (2010–2013)=== On January 10, 2011, Pavlović signed a 10-day contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=6007832|title=Mavericks sign Sasha Pavlovic|date=January 10, 2011|work=ESPN.com|access-date=October 18, 2020}} Pavlović started his first game for the Mavericks on the last day of his contract, scoring 11 points in the Mavericks' 109–100 win over the Lakers. On January 20, 2011, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Mavericks.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=6040688|title=Mavs re-sign Sasha Pavlovic|date=January 20, 2011|work=ESPN.com|access-date=October 18, 2020}} On January 30, 2011, his second 10-day contract expired and the Mavericks did not sign him for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=6073189|title=Mavs let Sasha Pavlovic go|date=January 30, 2011|work=ESPN.com|access-date=October 18, 2020}} On February 4, 2011, Pavlović signed a 10-day contract with the [[New Orleans Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_sign_sasha_pavlovic__2011_02_04.html|title=Hornets Sign Sasha Pavlovic to a 10-Day Contract|date=February 4, 2011|work=NBA.com|access-date=October 18, 2020}} On February 14, 2011, his contract expired and the Hornets did not sign him to a second 10-day contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2011/02/new_orleans_hornets_opt_not_to.html|title=New Orleans Hornets opt not to sign F Sasha Pavlovic to another 10-day contract|date=February 14, 2011|work=NOLA.com|access-date=February 14, 2011}} On March 3, 2011, Pavlović signed with the [[Boston Celtics]] for the rest of the 2010–11 season.[https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press030311-celtics-sign-pavlovic.html Celtics Sign Pavlovic] In his first appearance with Boston on March 6, 2011, in a game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], he played 12 minutes, going 1-for-2 from three and 1-for-3 field goals overall, recording 3 points and 2 steals. His contract expired following the [[2011 NBA playoffs|2011 playoffs]], and he returned to Montenegro to work out for the summer.{{cite news|url=http://www.csnne.com/blog/celtics-talk/pavlovic-happy-be-back-celtics|title=Pavlovic happy to be back with Celtics|date=December 12, 2011|work=CSNNE.com|access-date=December 25, 2011}} On December 12, 2011, upon the end of the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Pavlović re-signed with the Celtics.[https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/press121211-celtics-sign-pavlovic.html Celtics Sign Pavlovic] The [[2011–12 NBA season]] opened on [[Christmas Day]] 2011 and Pavlović started for an injured [[Paul Pierce]]. He played 15 minutes without attempting a shot or scoring a point.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=311225018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160804130945/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=311225018|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 4, 2016|title=Knicks need every ounce of Carmelo Anthony's 37 in win over Celtics|work=ESPN.com|date=December 25, 2011|access-date=October 18, 2020}} In the Celtics' second-last game of the season, a 78–66 win over the Heat, Pavlović scored 16 points off the bench.{{cite web|last=Robb|first=Brian|title=Notebook: Celtics 78, Heat 66|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/game.recap/04/24/heat-celtics/|work=NBA.com|date=April 25, 2012|access-date=April 25, 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222083011/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/game.recap/04/24/heat-celtics/|archive-date=February 22, 2014}} In 45 games (7 as starter), he averaged 2.7 points in 11.7 minutes per game. On July 20, 2012, Pavlović was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in a three-team deal.{{cite web | title = Rockets sign-and-trade Courtney Lee to Celtics in 3-team trade | url = http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10583 | work=InsideHoops.com | date = July 20, 2012 | access-date = October 18, 2020}} Pavlović' final NBA game was played on April 17, 2013, in an 88–99 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]] where he recorded 6 points and 1 rebound. On July 6, 2013, Pavlović was waived by the Trail Blazers.[https://www.blazersedge.com/2013/7/6/4499294/blazers-release-g-f-sasha-pavlovic Blazers Release G/F Sasha Pavlovic][https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/07/blazers-waive-sasha-pavlovic.html Blazers Waive Sasha Pavlovic] ===Partizan Belgrade (2014–2015)=== On February 10, 2014, Pavlović returned to Europe and officially signed with Serbian powerhouse [[KK Partizan|Partizan]] for the rest of the 2013–14 season.{{cite web|title=Sasha Pavlovic officially signs with Partizan Belgrade|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/serbia/73611/sasha-pavlovic-officially-signs-with-partizan-belgrade.html|work=Sportando.net|date=February 10, 2014|access-date=February 10, 2014}}{{cite web|title=Partizanova 'Osmica' - Aleksandar Pavlović! |url=http://www.kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest.php?id=1506 |work=KKPartizan.rs |language=sr |date=February 10, 2014 |access-date=February 10, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140301132306/http://www.kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest.php?id=1506 |archive-date=March 1, 2014 }} Partizan finished season by winning its 13th consecutive domestic title, defeating arch rivals [[KK Crvena zvezda|Red Star Belgrade]] by 3–1 in the final series.{{cite web|title=Ništa novo, Partizan je šampion!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=06&dd=21&nav_id=865626|website=b92.net|access-date=21 June 2014|language=sr}} In the final series he averaged 11.7 points and 2.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web|title=Pavlovic Aleksandar|url=http://kls.rs/igrac_stat.php?igrac=334|website=kls.rs|access-date=21 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140618205602/http://www.kls.rs/igrac_stat.php?igrac=334|archive-date=18 June 2014|url-status=dead}} Even though Pavlović was the most experienced player in the roster, it was his first championship win in his professional career. The day after the game, he said that winning a championship with Partizan was his greatest career accomplishment.{{cite web|title=Pavlović: Najveći uspeh u životu|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=06&dd=22&nav_id=865801|website=b92.net|access-date=22 June 2014|language=sr}} On December 1, 2014, Pavlović returned to Partizan and signed a contract for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Pavlović sa Partizanom u nove izazove! |url=http://www.kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest.php?id=1770 |access-date=1 December 2014 |work=kkpartizan.rs |date=1 December 2014 |language=sr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204030241/http://www.kkpartizan.rs/sr/vest.php?id=1770 |archive-date=4 December 2014 }} In the [[2014–15 ABA League|ABA League]] debut in the new season, he led his team in an 89–80 victory over [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Leks]] by scoring 26 points and having 4 rebounds and assists.{{cite news|title=Glorious return of Aleksandar Pavlović |url=http://www.abaliga.com/a8598/News/Glorious_return_of_Aleksandar_Pavlovic.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141208003311/http://www.abaliga.com/a8598/News/Glorious_return_of_Aleksandar_Pavlovic.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 December 2014 |access-date=8 December 2014 |work=abaliga.com }} Over 19 Adriatic League games, he averaged 11.9 points and 3.7 rebounds per game. ===Panathinaikos (2015–2016)=== On July 9, 2015, Pavlović signed a one-year contract with the Greek club [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]].{{cite news|title=Pavlovic: We agreed from the first call!!!|url=http://www.paobc.gr/page.ashx?pid=2&aid=43538&lang=2|access-date=9 July 2015|work=paobc.gr|date=9 July 2015}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} On April 21, 2016, he was released by the club.{{cite news|title=Kuzmic and Pavlovic replaced and released|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/heba/229745/kuzmic-and-pavlovic-replaced-and-released|access-date=21 April 2016|work=Eurohoops.net|date=21 April 2016}} ==International career== Pavlović was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-20 basketball team|Serbia and Montenegro Under-20]] national team and played at the [[2002 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship|2002 European Under-20 Championships]] in Lithuania. He was a member of the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia and Montenegro national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Olympic Games]], playing in four games, averaging 3.5 points and 1.8 rebounds. Two years later, Montenegro, his native country, [[2006 Montenegrin independence referendum|declared independence]] from the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro. After that, Pavlović said that he would like to play for the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national team]].[http://www.b92.net/sport/vesti.php?style=headlines&yyyy=2006&mm=07&dd=24&order=priority&nav_id=205632 Pavlović: "Igrao bih za Srbiju"] However, he did not play for the Serbian or the Montenegrin national team. When asked about a possible comeback in February 2014, he responded with: "I'm not thinking about the national team. To me, it became a political matter, not a sports matter. This is why I decided not to commit [to the national team]."{{cite news|last1=Bećagović|first1=M.|last2=Dinić|first2=M.|title=Pavlović: Daću sve da Partizan osvoji titulu, reprezentacija je političko pitanje|url=https://sport.blic.rs/Kosarka/Domaca-kosarka-i-ABA/247738/Pavlovic-Dacu-sve-da-Partizan-osvoji-titulu-reprezentacija-je-politicko-pitanje|access-date=5 December 2014|work=blic.rs|issue=11
